changelog:
**A restart no longer stops the television.** This is the oldest fault the plugin had, and it has been costing a stream every time anything was installed. The account channels play with identifies itself to the server with one fixed device id, and Jellyfin keeps one session per device id - so every time the plugin authenticated that account, it revoked the token whoever was already watching was using. The credentials were only ever held in memory, which meant a server restart, a plugin install, or simply a second television tuning in authenticated again and killed a stream that was playing. It did not look like an error either: the picture just loads for ever, because the stream's own requests are quietly being refused.

The token is now stored beside the account's password and checked before another one is asked for, so the usual case reuses the session already running and interrupts nothing. A token that turns out to belong to a different account is refused rather than used - renaming the playback account used to be able to leave one behind - and the log says on every path which of the two happened and what it cost.

Two things found while fixing it. **The account's password was being rewritten on every single request for credentials**, and changing a password is itself grounds for the server to revoke that account's tokens - so the cheap path was quietly creating the need for the expensive one. It is only written when the account is actually being authenticated now. And **pressing Save on the configuration page would have ended the stream**: a save carries the whole configuration, so any writer that did not know about the new field would have sent it back empty and wiped it, and the next tune-in would have authenticated afresh. That gap is filled in on the way through, the same way the trailer proof-of-origin token has been protected for a while.

Note for this one install: **it still costs a stream**, because there is no stored token yet. After this, restarts should be invisible to anything that is watching.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
